messages:
carla_support: Starting war room for hosted inference 5xx/timeouts affecting multiple customers in eu-west, noticed ~08:15 UTC. Customer ticket IDs: Z-3421, Z-3428. Initial symptom: sudden p50->p99 latency spike then 502/504s. Assigning @alex_sre oncall. :rotating_light:

alex_sre: I'm on it. Can someone drop a quick curl that reproduces the 502s? Also sharing current pager: https://pager.example/incident/1745009999

priya_cs: Customer reports errors when sending 10-30 concurrent requests. They saw long tail timeouts around 08:12-08:20 UTC. They downgraded client concurrency but still got intermittent 502s.

mina_eng: Looking at gateway logs now. I'm seeing repeated upstream connection resets and a small fraction of auth token refresh failures around 08:10-08:16. Could be auth proxy or connection pool exhaustion.

deploy-bot: [deploy] canary rollout 2026-03-17T07:58:03Z for routed-fallbacks completed -> 2026-03-17T08:05:10Z. 5% -> 20% -> aborted at 08:09 due to healthcheck flapping on eu-west-1.

alex_sre: Thanks. Mina, can you paste the relevant log snippet?

mina_eng: here's a short snippet: 
```
2026-03-17T08:11:23Z gateway[proxy]: upstream reset id=0x7f3a client=10.2.1.4 auth_refresh_error=0
2026-03-17T08:11:23Z auth-proxy: token-refresh failed status=503 retryable=true trace=abcd1234
2026-03-17T08:11:24Z gateway[proxy]: connection_pool_exhausted svc=hosted-inference region=eu-west svc_conn=16/16
```

alex_sre: Repro curl from support: 
```
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"input":"hello"}' --parallel 20
```
Produces 502/504 in ~30% of runs for the customer's traffic pattern.

carla_support: Customer also sent a stack trace showing client-side retries amplifying traffic. They used SDK v0.9.1 with default retry policy.

dave_pm: If SDK retries are amplifying during a deployment or small failure window that could explain the fanout -> upstream strain. We should mitigate quickly and then follow up with a tighter SDK backoff.

alex_sre: Immediate mitigations in progress: 
- rollback canary to previous routing config (in progress)
- temporarily throttle large concurrent requests per-customer at edge (rate limit patch rolling now)
- increase gateway circuit-breaker thresholds to avoid premature 502s

mina_eng: Rolling a quick patch to auth-proxy to fail-fast on token service 5xx (so we don't stall connections). Pushing now.

deploy-bot: [deploy] auth-proxy fail-fast patch queued -> 2026-03-17T08:22:01Z -> succeeded on eu-west canaries.

kb-alert-bot: Alert: p95 latency returned to baseline after throttling at 08:24 UTC. 5xx rate down from 18% -> 2% over 10m.

priya_cs: I've told the customers we're throttling heavy concurrency temporarily and working on root cause. They'll accept short throttles if we follow up with permanent fixes.

alex_sre: Root cause hypothesis: combined effect of a partial canary rollout + auth token refresh race + client retry amplification. Small auth-service spike caused many upstream auth failures -> gateway held connections -> client SDK retried in tight loop -> overload.

carla_support: Good summary. Let's capture action items and owners for postmortem and customer follow-up.

mina_eng: Action items I can own: 
- (A1) Add a fail-fast path in auth-proxy and backfill unit tests (owner: mina_eng) — ETA 2026-03-19
- (A2) Add a canary gate to block routing changes during auth-service instability (owner: mina_eng) — ETA 2026-03-24

alex_sre: My list: 
- (S1) Tune gateway circuit-breakers and connection-pool sizing for eu-west to raise graceful degradation thresholds (owner: alex_sre) — ETA 2026-03-20
- (S2) Add synthetic canary that runs concurrency profile (20-50 parallel requests) every 5m to detect regressions earlier (owner: alex_sre) — ETA 2026-03-18

dave_pm: Product/SDK changes: 
- (P1) Change SDK default retry policy to add jitter + exponential backoff and a max concurrency cap per-client (owner: dave_pm + devex) — ETA 2026-04-02
- (P2) Update SDK release notes and notify customers about recommended concurrency controls (owner: dave_pm) — ETA 2026-03-22

priya_cs: Customer comms: 
- (C1) Post incident summary and temporary mitigations (owner: priya_cs) — ETA 2026-03-18
- (C2) Offer a short credits package for impacted customers pending postmortem (owner: priya_cs) — ETA 2026-03-19

alex_sre: Short-term operational changes: 
- set an emergency runbook step to enable per-customer concurrency caps via edge in 5 clicks (doc update) (owner: alex_sre) — ETA 2026-03-16

mina_eng: I'll also instrument auth-proxy with a dedicated histogram for refresh latencies and a breakdown by client-id so we can spot noisy customers. (owner: mina_eng) — ETA 2026-03-18

carla_support: Postmortem meeting scheduled: 2026-03-18 15:00 UTC. Required attendees: alex_sre, mina_eng, dave_pm, priya_cs, carla_support. Draft will be posted to /docs/incidents/ after the meeting.

priya_cs: I'll prepare an initial customer-facing timeline for the meeting and include the mitigation steps we took.

alex_sre: Closing notes: major mitigation (throttle + rollback + auth-proxy fail-fast) reduced client impact within 10m. We should treat SDK retry policy as a top priority to avoid amplification.

carla_support: Thanks all. If anything else crops up ping this thread and escalation channel. I'll file the incident ticket and link to the postmortem doc after the 3/18 meeting. :white_check_mark:
